source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
Without a name, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; with a name, it is the mother of the myriad things.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A physical route or track for travel.
Sentence Translations (English): Travel on the road and do not lose the way.
At night, he returned along the road.
The cart broke down halfway along the road.
There is a narrow path in the mountains.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A practical way, procedure, or system for accomplishing something.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often emphasizes an effective or established manner of action.
Sentence Translations (English): There is a method for governing the state.
By learning the method, one can put it into practice.
This is the method of warfare.
Ask about his method, and you will know his skill.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To utter, express, or speak words.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): In older texts this can be a simple transitive verb of speaking.
Sentence Translations (English): I do not dare to speak of it in detail.
Since you have heard it, please say it again.
Everyone has words, but it is not easy to say it.
He then slowly recounted the matter.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The fundamental, all-encompassing principle or course by which reality is ordered and pursued; here, the metaphysical “Way” rather than a concrete road or a practical method.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Capitalized in English when treated as the text’s central philosophical term.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates that something is fit, proper, or worthy of a response or action.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often means “worth doing” or “appropriate,” not ability.
Sentence Translations (English): This matter must not be taken lightly, and the man is suitable for employment.
The gentleman judged it acceptable and then followed it.
His words are quite apt and enough to inform others.
When the time was fitting, then the rites were carried out.
Sentences: 此事不可小視，而其人可用。

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To agree to, approve, or grant assent to a proposal or action.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Typically implies sanctioning or allowing something to proceed.
Sentence Translations (English): The ruler approved the petition, and it was carried out.
Everyone thought it good and all approved it.
The Master did not answer at once; only after a long while did he consent.
When the discussion had been settled, the king also approved the plan.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Expresses possibility, ability, or permission in combination with a following verb or predicate.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this text it marks whether a term or description is applicable, not moral approval.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks something as mistaken, improper, or not right.
Sentence Translations (English): That statement is wrong and should be corrected.
This plan is already incorrect and cannot be carried out.
Knowing what is wrong is how one can return to the right.
The views of petty men often contain many errors.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To censure, find fault with, or denounce someone or something.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Focuses on censure or disapproval, not simple negation.
Sentence Translations (English): Everyone criticized his fault.
Do not criticize him over a small lapse.
When everyone in turn denounced him, he finally began to doubt himself.
The gentleman does not lightly criticize others.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A negative predicate used to deny that something belongs to a class or has a given property.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Negates classification or identity rather than simply adding emphasis.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The enduring, unchanging Way or principle, contrasted with what can be spoken or named only provisionally.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Philosophical and formulaic; refers to permanence rather than ordinary habit.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To give a name to someone or something; to call or label.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Requires an object that is being named.
Sentence Translations (English): The father named his son Bo.
Please name it.
The assembly had not yet decided, so they named this mountain.
Once the facts were obtained, they named it.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The standing or renown someone or something has among others.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Concerns public esteem or renown, not a literal label.
Sentence Translations (English): His fame was heard far among the lords.
His work was accomplished, yet his reputation was not prominent.
The gentleman values virtue and does not value reputation.
To become famous in one night is not necessarily lasting.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A word or designation by which a person, thing, or concept is called.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage it stands in contrast to the reality that naming can only partially capture.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A fixed, enduring name that would remain stable and fully adequate, unlike ordinary naming that varies with circumstance.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Philosophical and formulaic; points to permanence in naming.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The condition or idea of absolute absence, as a philosophical concept opposed to being.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Abstract metaphysical use, especially in early Chinese thought.
Sentence Translations (English): The myriad things are born from nonbeing.
The sage holds to nonbeing in order to observe its subtlety.
Being and nonbeing depend on each other and thus take shape.
Knowing the use of nonbeing, one then sees great skill.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks the absence of something, or says that something does not exist or is not present.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this context it negates possession or presence, not philosophical “nothingness.”

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The paired expression for the whole natural world or cosmos, conceived as the two great poles of reality.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A fixed binomial, not two separate nouns in ordinary coordination.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A third-person object pronoun referring back to a previously mentioned person or thing.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Usually refers to a known, contextually salient object.
Sentence Translations (English): On seeing the worthy, take him as a teacher.
After hearing his words, I believed him.
You may comfort him.
I cannot bear to abandon them.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A verb of motion meaning to go to, approach, or head toward a place or person.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Formal and literary in early texts; often directional or goal-oriented.
Sentence Translations (English): At dawn he went to the market.
Then he went to his gate.
All the ministers went to court.
He boarded a boat and went south.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A structural particle linking a noun phrase to a head noun or modifying phrase, expressing possession, attribution, or relation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks grammatical connection rather than lexical content.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To enter into existence or commence an action, process, or state.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Denotes actual inception, often with an object or complement.
Sentence Translations (English): Spring began this very morning.
Once the troops were arrayed, they began to march.
One does not act rashly in affairs; one must examine them before beginning.
When the people’s minds were settled, ritual and music then began to flourish.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The starting point, first stage, or source from which something comes forth.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Emphasizes the point of inception or origin rather than the act of beginning itself.
